entities.summary:
The Battle of Gaza may refer to multiple conflicts throughout history, but the most notable include the battles between Egypt and Macedon, Hasmonean Judea and Gaza/Nabateans, the Crusaders and the Ayyubids, and the Ottoman victory over the British. 

The Battle of Gaza of 2007 was a pivotal event in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. It was a turning point in the Second Intifada, marked by a massive Israeli military operation in the Gaza Strip.

The battle has been a recurring theme in the Middle East, with various dynasties and empires fighting for control. The legacy of the Battle of Gaza can be seen in the complex web of alliances and rivalries that continue to shape the region.

The 2007 Battle of Gaza remains a stark reminder of the ongoing conflict. Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak once quipped, 'We will never let the Gaza Strip be used as a launching pad for terror attacks.'

The Battle of Gaza has left an indelible mark on the history of the Middle East, with its echoes still resonating today.
